desc:
Smart product search for online stores understands what shoppers mean, handling typos, everyday words and plain requests. Ecom Swift LLC adds it to your store, so a search such as a warm jacket for hiking shows useful products instead of an empty page.

## What is smart product search?

Smart product search is a store search tool that works on meaning, not only on exact words. A basic search checks whether the typed word appears in a product title. A smarter one understands that "sneakers", "trainers" and "running shoes" can describe the same thing, forgives a spelling slip and ranks results by how well they fit the request.

It reads your product titles, descriptions and tags, and shows results as the shopper types. It also records searches that found nothing, which is information most stores never see.

## Why the search box is a high intent page

Shoppers who use search already know roughly what they want. They are often closer to buying than people who browse, and a failed search is the quickest way to lose them. A shopper who types a plural, a brand nickname or a misspelling and sees "no results" usually does not try again. They leave, and you never learn why.

Zero results also point to a vocabulary gap between your catalog and your customers. You may call it a "tote" while shoppers search for "shopping bag". Fixing that once helps every shopper who follows. How much this lifts sales depends on your products and traffic, but it removes a common cause of lost visits.

## What a good search setup includes

- Typo and plural handling, so small mistakes still find the product.
- A synonym list that matches how your customers speak.
- Instant results that update while the shopper types.
- Search by meaning, so descriptive requests return fitting products.
- Filters for price, color, size and other fields your catalog holds.
- Pinned results, so chosen products show first for chosen searches.
- Rules to boost a collection, such as new arrivals or items in stock.
- Search suggestions that appear as people type.
- A report of searches with no results.
- A layout tested on a phone, where most searching happens.

## How we work

We begin by looking at how your current search behaves. We try real searches, including misspellings and descriptive phrases, and record what fails. Then we read your catalog and decide which fields feed the search: titles, tags, descriptions and attributes.

Next we set up the search tool in your store, build a synonym list from your own vocabulary and test it on a set of realistic searches. We tune ranking so that in stock products with a close match come first, then we check the layout on mobile.

The Basic package improves matching for typos, synonyms and plurals with instant results. The Standard package adds search by meaning, filters, pinned products, the no results list and a mobile check. The Premium package adds suggestions while typing, merchandising rules, a larger synonym list, a test on a set of real searches and a weekly report. Some search tools carry a monthly fee set by their maker, and we tell you before you choose.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Review the no results list every month.
- Add synonyms for words your customers use, not only for your own terms.
- Keep product titles and attributes tidy, because search reads them.
- Test search on a phone as well as a computer.
- Pin products only where you have a clear reason.

**Avoid:**
- Boosting so many products that ranking stops making sense.
- Hiding the search box in a menu on mobile.
- Ignoring searches that return unrelated items.
- Adding a synonym without checking what it brings back.
- Relying on the search tool to fix thin product data.

## Who this is for

It suits a store with a growing catalog where the default search misses obvious matches. It suits an owner who sees shoppers leave after searching. It also suits a seller with products that have several common names.

## What we need from you

Share your store address, a short list of searches that fail today and any terms your customers use that differ from your titles. A product export helps. We never ask for passwords: access is given as a collaborator, staff or developer user, and we explain every change before we make it.
